docs.title: Bao - Benchmark and analysis of organoids
docs.text: Bao is a Python package designed for the benchmarking and analysis of organoids data. It provides tools for downloading an preparing publicly available datasets as well as a comprehensive set of classes to train neural networks on the different tasks.

docs.title: Handling the data
docs.text:
The bao.datasets subpackage handles everything relative to the supported datasets in the Bao package.

The bao.datasets.prepare_dataset function downloads the specified dataset and preprocesses it in the desired format. The name of the dataset should correspond to the name given in configs/dataset_config.yaml.

import bao

bao.datasets.prepare_dataset('tellu')

The bao.datasets.get_dataset_split function splits the samples into train and validation in a deterministic manner (given the seed), and returns test sample names if there is a predefined test set in the original dataset. This assumes that the dataset has already been downloaded and prepared, and is present in the directory given in data_dir (data by default).

import bao

train_names, val_names, test_names = bao.datasets.get_dataset_split(dataset_name='tellu',
                                                                    split=0,
                                                                    num_splits=4)

The bao.datasets.get_dataset function gives access to the specific dataset classes and initializes it.

import bao

train_names, _, _ = bao.datasets.get_dataset_split(dataset_name='tellu',
                                                   split=0,
                                                   num_splits=4)
train_dataset = bao.datasets.get_dataset(name='tellu',
                                         names=train_names,
                                         download=False, # has already been downloaded above
                                         mode='train', # mode should be train for train and val
                                         img_size=(1024, 1024))

All speicific dataset classes are also directly accessible.

import bao

train_names, _, _ = bao.datasets.get_dataset_split(dataset_name='tellu',
                                                   split=0,
                                                   num_splits=4)
train_dataset = bao.datasets.Tellu(names=train_names
                                   mode='train',
                                   img_size=(1024, 1024),
                                   download=False)

docs.title: Training and evaluating a model
docs.text:
The bao.train function is a packaged way of training your model. This can be done either by: - defining your torch.nn.Module model, which should output only the tensor output (i.e., no dictionary) - defining your lightning.LightningModule model, for which you can define your own losses (make sure to log at least 'train/loss' and 'val/loss')

The default hyperparameters for training are all defined in configs/train_config.yaml, if you wish to modify or add some hyperparameters, you may do so with the **kwargs.

Note: if you prefer to train a model using your own pipeline, you can always use the dataset classes defined above with your own pipeline.

import bao
import torch
import torchvision
# prepare the model to train
class WrapperModel(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, model):
        super(WrapperModel, self).__init__()
        self.model = model

    def forward(self, x):
        return torch.nn.functional.sigmoid(self.model(x)['out'])
model = WrapperModel(torchvision.models.segmentation.deeplabv3_resnet50(num_classes=1))
# train the model
bao.train(model, dataset_name='orgasegment', split=0, batch_size=8, optimizer_params={'lr': 0.01, 'weight_decay': 0.001})

The similar code works, providing a Lightning.LightningModule as input.

import bao
import torch
import torchvision
import lightning as L
# prepare the model to train
class CustomLightning(L.LightningModule):
    def __init__(self):
        super(CustomLightning, self).__init__() 
        self.loss = torch.nn.BCELoss()
        self.model = torch.nn.Sequential(torchvision.models.vgg16(), torch.nn.LazyLinear(1), torch.nn.Sigmoid())

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.model(x)

    def training_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        x, y = batch
        y_hat = self(x)
        loss = self.loss(y_hat, y)
        self.log('train/loss', loss, on_epoch=True, on_step=False, prog_bar=True)
        return loss

    def validation_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        x, y = batch
        y_hat = self(x)
        loss = self.loss(y_hat, y)
        self.log('val/loss', loss, on_epoch=True, on_step=False, prog_bar=True)
        return loss

    def configure_optimizers(self):
        return torch.optim.Adam(self.parameters(), lr=1e-4)

# train the model
model = CustomLightning()
bao.train(model, dataset_name='dcrypto_budding', split=0, download=True)

The bao.eval function evaluates a trained model on a specified dataset (which is already done at the end of the training), on the test set if one is present, or on the validation set. Similarly to bao.train, it can be applied on a torch.nn.Module or on a lightning.LightningModule.

import bao

model = WrapperModel(torchvision.models.segmentation.deeplabv3_resnet50(num_classes=1))
bao.eval(model, dataset_name='dcrypto_budding', split=0, download=False, checkpoint_path='/path/to/model.ckpt')

docs.title: Adding a new dataset to Bao
docs.text:
If a new open-source dataset has come out, feel free to add your implementation and create a pull request. Here are the steps necessary to handle a new dataset.

  1. Add the necessary information in bao/configs/dataset_config.yaml (download link, name, type of task, image size, number of classes).

  2. Create a function called prepare_<dataset_name> in bao/datasets/prepare_utils.py, which should create a .h5 file with the following structure for the train set (and same for test if there is a predefined test set).

    • classification: train/cls1, train/cls2, ...
    • segmentation: train/images and train/masks
    • detection: train/images and train/labels containing ([cls, start_x, start_y, end_x, end_y] arrays for the labels)
    • localization: train/images and train/labels containing ([start_x, start_y, end_x, end_y] arrays for the labels)

  3. Create the specific dataset class (e.g. if the dataset is for segmentation, in bao/datasets/segmentation_datasets.py which inherits from SegmentationDataset), and import it in bao/configs/__init__.py.

def prepare_dataset(dataset_name: str,
                    should_download: bool = True,
                    download_dir: str = '/tmp',
                    data_dir: str = default_data_dir) -> None:
    """Download and prepare the dataset with the given name.

        Args:
            dataset_name [str]: name of the dataset to prepare
            should_download [bool]: whether to download the dataset
            download_dir [str]: directory to download the dataset to
            data_dir [str]: directory to save the prepared dataset to

        Returns:
            None
    """
    from . import prepare_utils
    from .download import download, unzip
    from ..configs import dataset_config, default_data_dir

    assert dataset_name in dataset_config, f'Dataset {dataset_name} not found in dataset_configs.yaml.'

    download_url = dataset_config[dataset_name]['url']
    if isinstance(download_url, str):
        download_name = os.path.join(download_dir, f'{dataset_name}.zip')
        unziped_name = download_name.replace('.zip', '')
        if should_download:
            download(dataset_config[dataset_name].url, download_name)
            unzip(download_name, unziped_name)
    else:
        unziped_name = []
        for url in dataset_config[dataset_name].url:
            url, download_name = url
            download_name = os.path.join(download_dir, download_name)
            unziped_n = download_name.replace('.zip', '')
            unziped_name.append(unziped_n)
            if should_download:
                download(url, download_name)
                unzip(download_name, unziped_n)

    output_path = os.path.join(data_dir, f'{dataset_name}.h5')
    prepare_func = getattr(prepare_utils, f'prepare_{dataset_name}')
    prepare_func(unziped_name, output_path)

def get_dataset(name: str,
                data_dir: str = default_data_dir,
                **kwargs) -> Dataset:
    """Get the dataset for the given task.

        Args:
            name [str]: name of the dataset
            data_dir [str]: directory to the saved dataset
            kwargs: additional arguments to pass to the dataset

        Returns:
            dataset [torch.utils.data.Dataset]: dataset for the given task
    """
    if 'data_dir' in kwargs:
        data_dir = kwargs['data_dir']
        kwargs.pop('data_dir')

    if name == 'tellu':
        dataset = Tellu
    elif name == 'orgaquant':
        dataset = OrgaQuant
    elif name == 'multiorg':
        dataset = MultiOrg

    elif name == 'orgasegment':
        dataset = OrgaSegment
    elif name == 'orgaextractor':
        dataset = OrgaExtractor

    elif name == 'dcrypto_budding':
        dataset = DCryptOBudding
    elif name == 'dcrypto_opaque':
        dataset = DCryptOOpaque
    else:
        raise ValueError(f'Name {name} not supported.')
    return dataset(data_dir=data_dir, **kwargs)

def get_dataset_split(dataset_name: str,
                      split: int,
                      num_splits: int,
                      data_dir: str = default_data_dir,
                      seed: int = 0) -> None:
    """Get the names of the images in the dataset splits.

        Args:
            dataset_name [str]: name of the dataset to prepare
            split [int]: index of the split to get
            num_splits [int]: number of splits to create
            data_dir [str]: directory to save the prepared dataset to
            seed [int]: seed for the random number generator

        Returns:
            None
    """

    import h5py
    from ..configs import dataset_config, default_data_dir
    from sklearn.model_selection import KFold, StratifiedKFold

    assert dataset_name in dataset_config, f'Dataset {dataset_name} not found in dataset_configs.yaml.'

    dataset_path = os.path.join(data_dir, f'{dataset_name}.h5')
    dataset_type = dataset_config[dataset_name].task

    with h5py.File(dataset_path, 'r') as hdf:
        has_test = 'test' in hdf.keys()
        if dataset_type == 'classification':
            train_names = [os.path.join(cls, img) for cls in list(hdf.get('train').keys())
                           for img in list(hdf.get(os.path.join('train', cls)).keys())]
            test_names = [os.path.join(cls, img) for cls in list(hdf.get('test').keys())
                          for img in list(hdf.get(os.path.join('test', cls)).keys())] if has_test else None
            train_labels = [os.path.dirname(name) for name in train_names]
            splitter = StratifiedKFold(num_splits, random_state=seed, shuffle=True)
            train_idx, val_idx = list(splitter.split(train_names, train_labels))[split]
        else:
            train_names = list(hdf.get('train/images').keys())
            test_names = list(hdf.get('test/images').keys()) if has_test else None
            splitter = KFold(num_splits, random_state=seed, shuffle=True)
            train_idx, val_idx = list(splitter.split(train_names))[split]

    val_names = [train_names[i] for i in val_idx]
    train_names = [train_names[i] for i in train_idx]

    return train_names, val_names, test_names

class OrgaSegment(SegmentationDataset):
    def __init__(self,
                 names: list[str],
                 mode: str,
                 img_size: tuple[int],
                 download: bool,
                 download_dir: str = '/tmp',
                 data_dir: str = default_data_dir):
        """Initialize the OrgaSegment dataset for segmentation.\nOriginal paper available at
        [https://www.nature.com/articles/s42003-024-05966-4](https://www.nature.com/articles/s42003-024-05966-4){:target="_blank"}.

            Args:
                names [list]: list of image names
                mode [str]: mode of the dataset in (train, test), should be train for train and val
                img_size [tuple]: size of the images
                download [bool]: whether to download the dataset
                download_dir [str]: directory to download the dataset to
                data_dir [str]: directory to save the prepared dataset to
        """
        if download:
            prepare_dataset('orgasegment', data_dir=data_dir, download_dir=download_dir)
        super().__init__('orgasegment', names, mode, img_size, data_dir)

def train(model: Module,
          dataset_name: str,
          split: int,
          download: bool,
          download_dir: str = '/tmp',
          data_dir: str = default_data_dir,
          num_splits: int = 4,
          **kwargs) -> None:
    """Train a model on a specified dataset.

        Args:
            model [torch.nn.Module | L.LightningModule]: model to train
            dataset_name [str]: name of the dataset to train on
            split [int]: index of the split to train on
            download_dir [str]: directory to download the dataset to
            download [bool]: whether to download the dataset
            data_dir [str]: directory to save the prepared dataset to
            num_splits [int]: number of splits to create
            kwargs: additional arguments to update the training configuration

        Returns:
            None
    """
    from ..datasets import get_dataset_split
    from ..configs import train_config, dataset_config
    import torch
    import lightning as L
    from .models import get_model
    from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
    from .train_utils import update_easydict
    from ..datasets import get_dataset
    from ..datasets import prepare_dataset
    from lightning.pytorch.callbacks import EarlyStopping, ModelCheckpoint

    updated_train_config = update_easydict(train_config, kwargs)
    L.seed_everything(updated_train_config.seed, workers=True)

    assert dataset_name in dataset_config, f'Dataset {dataset_name} not found in dataset_configs.yaml.'

    if not isinstance(model, L.LightningModule):
        model = get_model(dataset_config[dataset_name].task)(model,
                                                             updated_train_config.optimizer,
                                                             updated_train_config.optimizer_params,
                                                             dataset_config[dataset_name].num_classes)

    img_size = dataset_config[dataset_name].size
    if download:
        prepare_dataset(dataset_name=dataset_name, download_dir=download_dir, data_dir=data_dir)
    train_names, val_names, test_names = get_dataset_split(dataset_name=dataset_name,
                                                           split=split,
                                                           num_splits=num_splits,
                                                           data_dir=data_dir,
                                                           seed=updated_train_config.seed)

    train_dataset = get_dataset(name=dataset_name,
                                data_dir=data_dir,
                                names=train_names,
                                download=False,
                                mode='train',
                                img_size=img_size)
    val_dataset = get_dataset(name=dataset_name,
                              data_dir=data_dir,
                              names=val_names,
                              download=False,
                              mode='train',
                              img_size=img_size)
    test_dataset = get_dataset(name=dataset_name,
                               data_dir=data_dir,
                               names=test_names,
                               download=False,
                               mode='test',
                               img_size=img_size) if test_names is not None else None

    collate_fn = getattr(model, 'collate_fn', None)
    train_dataloader = DataLoader(train_dataset,
                                  batch_size=updated_train_config.batch_size,
                                  shuffle=True,
                                  num_workers=updated_train_config.num_workers,
                                  collate_fn=collate_fn)
    val_dataloader = DataLoader(val_dataset,
                                batch_size=updated_train_config.batch_size,
                                shuffle=False,
                                num_workers=updated_train_config.num_workers,
                                collate_fn=collate_fn)
    test_dataloader = DataLoader(test_dataset,
                                 batch_size=updated_train_config.batch_size,
                                 shuffle=False,
                                 num_workers=updated_train_config.num_workers,
                                 collate_fn=collate_fn) if test_names is not None else None

    early_stopping = EarlyStopping(monitor='val/loss',
                                   patience=updated_train_config.patience)
    model_checkpoint = ModelCheckpoint(monitor='val/loss', mode='min', save_last=False, save_top_k=1)
    callbacks = [early_stopping, model_checkpoint]
    trainer = L.Trainer(max_epochs=updated_train_config.max_epochs,
                        callbacks=callbacks,
                        accelerator='cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu',
                        devices=1,
                        log_every_n_steps=1)
    trainer.fit(model,
                train_dataloader,
                val_dataloader)

    trainer.validate(model,
                     test_dataloader if test_names is not None else val_dataloader,
                     ckpt_path=model_checkpoint.best_model_path)

def eval(model: Module,
         dataset_name: str,
         split: int,
         checkpoint_path: str,
         download: bool,
         download_dir: str = '/tmp',
         data_dir: str = default_data_dir,
         num_splits: int = 4) -> None:
    """Evaluate a trained model on a specified dataset.

        Args:
            model [torch.nn.Module | L.LightningModule]: model to evaluate
            dataset_name [str]: name of the dataset to evaluate on
            split [int]: index of the split to evaluate on
            checkpoint_path [str]: path to the model checkpoint
            download [bool]: whether to download the dataset
            download_dir [str]: directory to download the dataset to
            data_dir [str]: directory to save the prepared dataset to
            num_splits [int]: number of splits to create

        Returns:
            None
    """
    import torch
    import lightning as L
    from .models import get_model
    from ..datasets import get_dataset
    from ..datasets import prepare_dataset
    from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
    from ..datasets import get_dataset_split
    from ..configs import train_config, dataset_config

    L.seed_everything(train_config.seed, workers=True)

    assert dataset_name in dataset_config, f'Dataset {dataset_name} not found in dataset_configs.yaml.'

    if download:
        prepare_dataset(dataset_name=dataset_name, download_dir=download_dir, data_dir=data_dir)

    if not isinstance(model, L.LightningModule):
        model = get_model(dataset_config[dataset_name].task)(model,
                                                            train_config.optimizer,
                                                            train_config.optimizer_params,
                                                            dataset_config[dataset_name].num_classes)

    img_size = dataset_config[dataset_name].size
    _, val_names, test_names = get_dataset_split(dataset_name=dataset_name,
                                                 split=split,
                                                 num_splits=num_splits,
                                                 data_dir=data_dir,
                                                 seed=train_config.seed)

    test_names = test_names if test_names is not None else val_names
    test_dataset = get_dataset(dataset_config[dataset_name].task,
                               dataset_name=dataset_name,
                               data_dir=data_dir,
                               names=test_names,
                               mode='test',
                               img_size=img_size)
    collate_fn = getattr(model, 'collate_fn', None)
    test_dataloader = DataLoader(test_dataset,
                                 batch_size=train_config.batch_size,
                                 shuffle=False,
                                 num_workers=train_config.num_workers,
                                 collate_fn=collate_fn)

    trainer = L.Trainer(accelerator='cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu',
                        devices=1)

    trainer.validate(model,
                     test_dataloader,
                     ckpt_path=checkpoint_path)
